description: One shared Cartesian frame. The horizontal axis extends a short distance left of its intersection with the vertical axis and has a rightward positive arrow. The vertical axis extends a short distance below the intersection and has an upward positive arrow. No negative-end arrow is visible.

One continuous solid unmarked curve begins at the axes' intersection, rises steeply in the positive-positive quadrant, then becomes progressively flatter toward its right endpoint. It stops well before the horizontal-axis arrow. There is no return branch, curve arrow, explicit saturation marker, labelled point, horizontal asymptote, dashed curve or shaded region. The curve shares the axes' origin, remains in the positive-positive quadrant, increases monotonically and approaches a nearly horizontal, nonzero terminal slope. Axes are perpendicular. Approximate source-screen positions are intersection (56,347) and curve endpoint (360,100); these are visual-location observations, not measured magnetic coordinates. One renderer-native cubic path is modern smooth-line regularization, not experimental data. The same two unmeasured cubic controls are preserved from the initial attempt; no curve labels, ticks, points or measurements are embedded in the path.

I, at the upper left of the vertical positive end. B with a subscript 0, below the horizontal positive end; no vector accent. An italic zero-shaped origin glyph immediately below-left of the intersection, preserved as 0. No intentional scale ticks, numbered graduations, units or grid. Small irregular marks on the scanned strokes are print noise, not added ticks.
